# PR 3142 loaded completion fixture

Experimental harness work; do not merge this branch. Local smoke validates the fixture only. No hosted comparison is dispatched by this plan or by a successful smoke.

## Workload and measurement boundaries

One Dekaf producer and consumer share a process and a fresh Kafka 4.3.1 topic. The producer uses Acks.All, idempotence, 5 ms linger, 128 KiB batches, 64 MiB BufferMemory and one fixed connection per broker. The consumer uses manual partition assignment and manual offset commits. Application payloads are byte arrays; the production byte-array deserializer's allocations remain included in process allocation totals.

The load is closed-loop saturation with 1,024 preallocated message slots. A slot is reusable only after both its delivery callback and consumer handling finish. There is one producer loop; no external open-loop arrival rate is claimed. The timestamp starts before waiting for a free slot, so application backpressure and producer queueing are included. Delivery latency ends in the successful broker acknowledgment callback. Completion latency ends after the consumer validates the payload sequence and offset. Both histograms record every completed message, including maxima and overflow counts. Per-partition sequence numbers detect missing, duplicate or reordered records; sent, acknowledged and consumed counts must match exactly, and all slots must return.

The fixture exercises producer and consumer networking together. CPU time and allocation scope is the entire client process, including both clients, the load loop, bounded channel, timestamps, histograms and sampler. Broker CPU must be retained separately. This combined result cannot attribute a CPU change to one client independently. It also does not replace the pool microbenchmark's MemoryDiagnoser result or the separate throwing-reservation cleanup test.

Each fresh process runs the same workload during an elapsed warmup phase, drains all warmup work, then measures using the same clients. Warmup and measured histograms/counters are preallocated separately. One-second samples retain completion counts, process CPU, allocations, GC, heap/RSS, JIT activity, thread-pool state and cumulative delivery/completion latency. The measurement ends only after final acknowledgment and consumer completion; the tail drain has a 30-second ceiling. CPU/allocation totals stop before report serialization and client disposal. Sampler work during the measurement is included equally in every phase. No sample, maximum or startup spike is removed.

## Intended hosted campaign

Before dispatch, fetch main, pin A, verify exact candidate B contains A, and record exact harness/product SHAs. Build both products and validate the same fixture against both before timing. Use a single ubuntu-latest VM; reserve separate broker/client CPU sets, record hardware/image/SDK/runtime, stop build servers, and execute A1 / B / A2 sequentially. Reset broker/container/topic/application state consistently for every phase. All phases must have identical Release/runtime/JIT/GC, fixture, inputs and profiling settings.

Representative configurations: 1,000-byte messages across three partitions, and 65,536-byte messages on one partition. Predeclare 60 seconds of elapsed workload warmup and 300 seconds measured per configuration and process. This five-minute window tests sustained completion and backlog behavior, not an hours-long leak hypothesis. Record broker resource usage and client termination/leftover work. Any additional configuration or changed duration needs a revised predeclared plan before its measurements.

Protected scalar metrics are completed throughput, both latency distributions' p50/p99/max, process CPU per completed message, process allocated bytes per completed message, and stability of backlog/GC/heap/RSS over time. The intended numerical screen is a 3% adverse tolerance against each within-run control, with control drift above 3% inconclusive. These thresholds are prospective, not chosen from loaded results. Report absolute A1/B/A2 values, both candidate deltas, drift and sample counts; assess uncertainty using time blocks rather than assuming millions of latency observations are independent. Missing metrics, inadequate precision, histogram overflow, persistent startup transitions or growing backlog make acceptance INCONCLUSIVE. A confirmed protected-metric loss is REGRESSION; no unrelated gain offsets it. Zero failures, exact completion agreement and no leftover slots are correctness prerequisites.

Do not infer a formal performance PASS from the scalar screen alone. The current implementation is under fixture validation: the hosted driver, broker CPU series, bounded failure/shutdown validation, uncertainty calculation, fresh-main microbenchmark comparison and cold cleanup-path evidence remain to be completed. Any result missing these applicable requirements remains INCONCLUSIVE. Keep scheduled stress coverage and paid lanes unchanged. No identical paid repeat is authorized here.

## Local smoke

Three seconds of warmup plus five measured seconds is deliberately below acceptance warmup. It tests both message configurations, all-message latency counts, exact completion and slot recovery against a newly owned Kafka container. The first launcher attempt used mismatched listener/advertised ports and failed readiness before running the client; its logs are retained. The corrected launcher binds the same selected port inside and outside the owned container. Only the container created by that launcher is removed.
